newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM SETS TENDER FOR STATE NOTES.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM SETS TENDER FOR STATE NOTES.

text.p: The Belgian Treasury is tendering further issues of 3/5/7 year and 5/7 year state notes, it said in an announcement on Tuesday.
Coupons will be announced on August 18. Subscriptions open on August 26 and close on September 3. Payment is due on September 4.

The Treasury said it would consider re-opening its two June issues if market conditions were unchanged with a short, nine-month first coupon to have matching payment dates for coupon and final maturity for the June and September issues.
The issues would thus become fungible after the payment of the first coupon, the same procedure as for the 246 and 274 "Philippes" state loans.
The five-year note, extendable to seven years, issued in June had a fixed, 4.70 percent, coupon.
The revisable rate note had an initial guaranteed minimum 3.85 percent coupon, rising to 4.70 percent at five years and to 5.35 percent at seven years.
Both issues were sold at par.

The June issues raised 8.175 billion francs. Belgium hopes to raise 54 billion francs from a total of four note issues planned for 1997/1998. Last year it raised 53 billion francs when it had targeted 80 billion.
The state notes are aimed at retail investors in direct competition with commercial banks' savings, or "cash", bonds, traditionally Belgium's most popular investment vehicle.
